name: dev-tools
description: Development tooling for Claude Code: the autonomous dev loop stack, CSS/design-drift auditing, mobile platform (iOS HIG + Material 3) guidelines, and shared-database discipline for one-instance-many-projects setups.

plugins.name: loop-stack
plugins.description: Universal, config-driven autonomous dev loop stack: session crons that fix assigned bugs, implement sprint stories behind a mandatory architect brief, verify against AC + deploys, review requested PRs, shepherd your own PRs to merge, repair failed deployments, sync fix-base branches, sweep a small time-boxed batch of e2e scenarios per tick into a rolling suite-health report, and post a daily standup report. Project specifics live in .claude/stack.md (written by the onboard skill). Optionally delegates shared disciplines (TDD, debugging, verification, code review) to the superpowers plugin when installed. Plus the on-demand SDLC intake pipeline (/sdlc): sweep the whole tracker + docs space into a resumable corpus, index it (qdrant/pgvector, optional graphify graph), harvest it in depth, and synthesize Requirements, Designs, a PRD, and a Task Master dev plan.

plugins.name: css-drift-auditor
plugins.description: Universal, framework-agnostic CSS/design-drift audit pipeline: maps components and raw HTML tags, renders components in Storybook, extracts post-cascade computed styles, and flags inconsistent values for tokenization.

plugins.name: mobile-platform-guidelines
plugins.description: Apple Human Interface Guidelines (HIG) and Android Material Design 3 rules for building native-feeling mobile UI: audits screens, components, navigation, permissions, and notifications against the relevant platform reference before implementation.

plugins.name: shared-database-discipline
plugins.description: Rules for running one shared Postgres/MongoDB behind many projects instead of a database container per repo: per-environment isolation enforced with REVOKE rather than convention, a three-role credential model where apps never run as owner, connection-string formats that silently break (Npgsql rejects postgresql:// URIs; semicolon values must not be shell-sourced), and self-hosted-runner deploy safety.
